title: Selected-scenario score equation silently drops non-finite lambda terms, so displayed addends need not equal displayed score
description: The selected-scenario callout renders a literal equation `objective <objective> + lambda <name> <value> ... = score <decision_score>`. The addends come from `selectedLambdaEntries = finiteRecordEntries(selected?.lambda_terms)`, which filters out any lambda term that is not a finite number (optimiserApplyHelpers.ts:18-21). The right-hand side `selected.decision_score` is rendered verbatim. If `lambda_terms` contains a non-finite term (NaN/Inf sentinel, which the formatValue layer explicitly models), that term is omitted from the shown sum while still being reflected in the backend `decision_score`, so the rendered equation does not visually add up (objective + shown_terms != shown_score). The plus-separated layout presents this as an arithmetic identity, so the silent omission is misleading rather than merely incomplete. Showing the term (e.g. as NaN/Infinity, consistent with formatValue's sentinel handling) would keep the equation faithful.
evidence: Line 41 `const selectedLambdaEntries = finiteRecordEntries(selected?.lambda_terms)`; helpers:18-21 `finiteRecordEntries` keeps only entries where `isFiniteNumber(entry[1])`. Lines 80-92 render `{objectiveLabel}{selected.objective}` then `selectedLambdaEntries.map(([name,value]) => ...'+ lambda name value')` then `=score {selected.decision_score}` — the LHS omits any non-finite lambda term while the RHS shows the full decision_score.
